## BLUF

It is not exactly simple, but also not too hard, to connect price and length data for black sea bass. Hopefully it will become easier as the cflen_aa table is replaced with something better (see JIRA [CAMSNR-1236](https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/jira/browse/CAMSNR-1236)).

## Black Sea Bass Bottom Line

Here is an example of how to connect black sea bass price and length measurements by market category.

```{r}

mysql <- "with tmplen as
(
  select camsid, area , nespp4, length, numlen
  from cams_garfo.cams_cflen_aa
  where itis_tsn = '167687' -- bsb
 /* and area in (614, 615, 621, 622, 623, 624, 625, 626, 627, 628, 629, 631, 632, 633, 634, 635, 636, 637, 638, 639, 640) -- southern */
  and year = 2024
), tmpland as
(
  select camsid, dlr_mkt, livlb, value, 
    case when dlr_mkt = 'LG' then '3351'
         when dlr_mkt = 'JB' then '3352'
         when dlr_mkt = 'MD' then '3353'
         when dlr_mkt = 'SQ' then '3355'
         when dlr_mkt = 'ES' then '3356'
       else '3350' end as nespp4
  from cams_garfo.cams_land
  where itis_tsn = '167687' -- bsb
/*  and area in (614, 615, 621, 622, 623, 624, 625, 626, 627, 628, 629, 
               631, 632, 633, 634, 635, 636, 637, 638, 639, 640) -- southern */
  and year = 2024
), tmpland2 as
(
  select camsid, dlr_mkt, nespp4, sum(livlb) as livlb, sum(nvl(value,0)) as value
  from tmpland
  group by camsid, dlr_mkt, nespp4
)
select e.camsid, e.nespp4, a.dlr_mkt, e.length, e.numlen, e.area, a.livlb, a.value, 
  round(a.value/a.livlb, 3) as priceperlb
from tmplen e
left join tmpland2 a
on e.camsid = a.camsid and e.nespp4 = a.nespp4
order by e.camsid, e.nespp4"
  
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, mysql)
bigdat <- fetch(rs)
bigdat<-bigdat %>%
  mutate(
    STOCK_ABBREV = case_when(
      AREA >= 621 & AREA<=639 ~ "SOUTH",
      AREA %in% c(614, 615)   ~ "SOUTH",
      AREA %in% c(464,465,467,468,510,511,512,513,514,515) ~ "NORTH",
      AREA %in% c(520,521,522,523,524,525,526,530,533,534,537,538,539,541,542) ~ "NORTH",
      AREA %in% c(543,551,552,560,561,562,611,612,613,616)~ "NORTH",
      AREA %in% c(0,000) ~ "UNK",
      .default = "UNK"
    )
  )

ggplot(filter(bigdat, !is.na(DLR_MKT)), aes(x=PRICEPERLB, y=LENGTH, color=DLR_MKT)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = NUMLEN), alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    trans = "log10",
    range = c(1, 3), # Controls min and max point sizes on the plot
    name = "Number of Lengths (log scale)"
  ) +
  labs(x="Price per Pound ($)", y="Length (cm)", title="Southern Black Sea Bass in 2024") +
  theme_bw()
```


```{r}
#Facet Wrapped over STOCK ABBREV
ggplot(filter(bigdat, !is.na(DLR_MKT), STOCK_ABBREV !="UNK"), aes(x=PRICEPERLB, y=LENGTH, color=DLR_MKT)) +
    facet_wrap(vars(STOCK_ABBREV)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = NUMLEN), alpha = 0.4) +
    scale_size_continuous(
      trans = "log10",
      range = c(1, 3), # Controls min and max point sizes on the plot
      name = "Number of Lengths (log scale)"
    ) +
    labs(x="Price per Pound ($)", y="Length (cm)", title="Black Sea Bass in 2024") +
    theme_bw()
  
```

```{r}
# how many distinct CAMSID?
  bigdat2 %>%
    group_by(STOCK_ABBREV) %>%
    summarise(count=n_distinct(CAMSID))
```

## How Did I Get Here?

First need to figure out the ITIS code for black sea bass and areas associated with one of the regions. I used cfg_itis for the former and looked at StockEff website for the latter.

```{r}
mysql <- "select itis_tsn, itis_name, itis_sci_name from cams_garfo.cfg_itis
where itis_name like '%BASS%'"

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, mysql)
dat <- fetch(rs)
knitr::kable(dat)
```

Now get the landings and prices for southern BSB in 2024.

```{r}
mysql <- "select dlr_mkt, sum(livlb) as sumlbs, sum(value) as sumvalue
from cams_garfo.cams_land
where itis_tsn = '167687' -- bsb
and area in (614, 615, 621, 622, 623, 624, 625, 626, 627, 628, 629, 
             631, 632, 633, 634, 635, 636, 637, 638, 639, 640) -- southern
and year = 2024
group by dlr_mkt
order by dlr_mkt"

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, mysql)
dat <- fetch(rs)
knitr::kable(dat)
```

Need to figure out NESPP4 for BSB because cams_garfo.cams_cflen_aa uses NESPP4 instead of market and grade (ugh).

```{r, eval=FALSE}
mysql <- "select c.*, m.market_desc, g.grade_desc 
from stockeff.I_CF_NESPP4_C c
left join nefsc_garfo.cfdbs_safismarket m
on c.market_code = m.market_code 
left join bsm.bsm_accsp_grade_categories g
on c.grade_code = g.grade_code
where species_itis = '167687'
order by nespp4"

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, mysql)
dat <- fetch(rs)
knitr::kable(dat)
```

Now pull the southern BSB lengths for 2024.

```{r}
mysql <- "select camsid, nespp4, length, numlen 
from cams_garfo.cams_cflen_aa
where itis_tsn = '167687' -- bsb
and area in (614, 615, 621, 622, 623, 624, 625, 626, 627, 628, 629, 
             631, 632, 633, 634, 635, 636, 637, 638, 639, 640) -- southern
and year = 2024"

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, mysql)
dat <- fetch(rs)
knitr::kable(head(dat))
```

Summarize the number of lengths by market category.

```{r}
datsum <- dat |>
  group_by(NESPP4) |>
  summarize(sumnumlen = sum(NUMLEN), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(datsum)
```

Linking the length and price data results in the big data pull that is used to create the main plot above.
